subject.title: PR3/5 durable core: wake targets, producers, and replay

question: Should this new durable-core architecture be accepted into OpenClaw core and landed on the release/2026.7.1 line before its prerequisite stack items are merged?
rationale: The PR adds persistent shared-state schema and replay/message-routing semantics whose release placement and long-term ownership cannot be inferred from tests or contributor intent.

options.title: Land sequentially on main
options.body: Approve the architecture in principle, merge prerequisites first on main, require upgrade and live replay proof, then choose a later release train.

options.title: Approve the release branch
options.body: Explicitly accept the schema and runtime risk for release/2026.7.1 and require exact merged-stack proof before landing.

options.title: Pause the durable stack
options.body: Keep the current runtime model and close or redesign the stack if maintainers do not want another core orchestration layer.

recommendation.title: Land sequentially on main
recommendation.body: Approve the architecture in principle, merge prerequisites first on main, require upgrade and live replay proof, then choose a later release train.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a core architecture and release-train acceptance decision.
